name: Chelubai
overview: Chelubai is a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, known specifically as the son of Hezron and grandson of Perez, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:9. Beyond this genealogical note, Scripture provides limited additional information about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Chelubai means 'dog; snappish warding off,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with connotations of vigilance or protection. A related name, Caleb, shares a similar meaning, indicating a thematic link in naming within this lineage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Chelubai as the son of Hezron. Additional inferred relationships within the broader family include connections to individuals such as Azubah, Jerioth, Jesher, Shobab, and others, suggesting a complex family network, though direct ties to Chelubai beyond his father are not explicitly stated.
scriptureSignificance: Chelubai's significance lies primarily in his place within the Messianic lineage of Judah through Perez and Hezron, underscoring the faithfulness of God's covenantal promises to Israel's patriarchs. While not elaborated upon in narrative detail, his genealogical position connects to the broader story of God's providential preservation of the tribe of Judah, from which Christ would ultimately come.
